node.title: Re: Old Programmer New To Perl
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Welcome to Perl and PerlMonks!

I much prefer to do my own research. Asking questions, like here, is a last resort.

I feel the same, but there's also no need to be worried about posting here.

I was told by some folks at mersenneforum.org that membership here can be tough.

Well, sometimes, but in my experience only when people are rude, spread bad information, and/or treat PM as a code writing service instead of a place to learn Perl. If you show your code ([id://1177642|SSCCE]), your thought process, and that you're learning from the replies you get, then as a general rule you should get a lot of help :-) Have a look at [id://213052] and [id://174051], and feel free to ask here anytime!

Some things to get started:

  • [doc://perlintro]
  • [id://832725]
  • [id://1174878]

My personal book recommendations for a programmer new to Perl would be: [http://shop.oreilly.com/product/0636920018452.do|Learning Perl] (optional depending on programming skill level), [http://modernperlbooks.com/books/modern_perl_2016/|Modern Perl], and of course [http://shop.oreilly.com/product/9780596004927.do|The Camel].
